title: How to Register BIR Books of Accounts
description: Register and maintain your mandatory manual or digital books of accounts for tax compliance in the Philippines.

requirements.title: BIR COR (Form 2303)
requirements.description: A photocopy of your BIR Certificate of Registration.

requirements.title: Valid ID
requirements.description: A government-issued ID of the taxpayer.

requirements.title: ORUS Account
requirements.description: An active account on the BIR Online Registration and Update System portal.

checklist.title: Choose Format
checklist.description: Decide between manual, loose-leaf, or computerized books of accounts.

checklist.title: Prepare Books
checklist.description: Purchase the required number of manual columnar books from an office supply store.

checklist.title: Register via ORUS
checklist.description: Log in to the ORUS portal and input the details of your books to register them.

checklist.title: Download QR Stamp
checklist.description: Generate and print the digital QR Code Stamp for each of your registered books.

checklist.title: Affix Stamps
checklist.description: Paste the printed QR stamps on the inside front cover of your manual books.

content.title: What are BIR Books of Accounts?

blocks.content: **Books of Accounts** are mandatory records where all business transactions are recorded for tax purposes. Every registered taxpayer in the Philippines (individual or corporation) is required to maintain these books to ensure accurate reporting of income and expenses.

The Books of Accounts are commonly used for:
*   Recording daily sales and expenses
*   BIR audits and tax assessments
*   Financial reporting and monitoring

You may need to register Books of Accounts if you are:
- A self-employed professional (freelancer, doctor, lawyer)
- A sole proprietor (Sari-sari store, online seller, etc.)
- A corporation or partnership
- Any entity issued a BIR Certificate of Registration (COR)

content.title: Benefits of Registered Books of Accounts

blocks.content: Maintaining proper books is not just a legal requirement; it helps manage your business better.

blocks.title: Tax Compliance
blocks.content: Avoid heavy penalties (ranging from ₱1,000 to ₱50,000) for failure to keep or register books.

blocks.title: Financial Clarity
blocks.content: Properly kept books allow you to see exactly where your money is going, making it easier to file your quarterly and annual income tax returns.

blocks.title: Online (ORUS)
blocks.content: The BIR now requires taxpayers to register their books through the **ORUS portal** to receive a digital **QR Code Stamp**.

blocks.title: Walk-In (RDO)
blocks.content: You may still need to visit your Revenue District Office (RDO) if the online system is unavailable or for specific manual stamping requirements.
**Pro Tip:** Use the BIR **eFPS or eBIRForms** for faster filing and avoid manual queuing at the RDO. Most payments can now be done via GCash or Maya.

blocks.title: Choose Your Format
blocks.content:
*   **Manual:** Handwritten (best for small businesses).
*   **Loose-Leaf:** Encoded on computer, printed, and bound (requires a Permit to Use).
*   **Computerized (CAS):** System-generated (best for large corporations).

blocks.title: Buy and Prepare Manual Books
blocks.content: If choosing manual, buy the 4 or 6 columnar books. Fill out the "Taxpayer Information" on the first page of each book.

blocks.title: Register via ORUS
blocks.content: Log in to [orus.bir.gov.ph](https://orus.bir.gov.ph). Select **Secondary Registration** > **Register Books of Accounts**. Input the details of your books (type, volume number, and number of pages).

blocks.title: Download the QR Stamp
blocks.content: Once submitted, the system will generate a **QR Code Stamp** for each book. Download and print these stamps.

blocks.title: Affix the Stamps
blocks.content: Paste the QR Code Stamp on the **inside front cover** or the **first page** of each corresponding manual book. Your books are now officially registered!

Applicants may process their Books of Accounts at:
- [BIR ORUS Portal](https://orus.bir.gov.ph)
- Your assigned **Revenue District Office (RDO)**

Typical processing timelines include:
*   Online (ORUS): Instant to 24 Hours
*   Manual (RDO): Same Day (if walk-in is allowed)
You can view your registered books and their QR stamps at any time by logging into your **ORUS account**.

Applicants may experience:
- **ORUS System Downtime:** The portal may occasionally be offline for maintenance.
- **Wrong RDO:** Attempting to register books when your record is still at a different RDO.

items: **Registering Late:** Books must be registered **before** you start business operations.
**Messy Entries:** For manual books, ensure entries are legible. Erasures should be avoided or initialed.

blocks.content: Always keep your books updated. The BIR requires entries to be made daily or at the end of each month.

items: Use the ORUS portal instead of going to the RDO to save time.
Make sure you have a clear scanned copy of your COR before starting the online application.
If you are a freelancer, Manual Books are the simplest and cheapest option to maintain.

blocks.content:
For the most accurate and up-to-date information, please refer to:
*   [Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR)](https://www.bir.gov.ph)
*   [BIR Online Registration and Update System (ORUS)](https://orus.bir.gov.ph)

blocks.title: Do I need to register new books every year?
blocks.content: No. For manual books, you only register a new set once the current volumes are completely full.

blocks.title: Can I use Excel as my books?
blocks.content: You can, but this is classified as **Loose-Leaf** or **Computerized** and requires prior approval (Permit to Use) from the BIR before you can use it for official records.
